text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this morning.
GAZETA MERCANTIL
-- GOVT POSTPONES CVRD AUCTION

The government has decided to postpone the entire schedule for the privatization of state mining giant CVRD, which means the company's minimum price will not be published December 17 and the auction will be later than mid-February.
-- EXPORTS FALL 7 PERCENT IN NOVEMBER VS OCTOBER
November exports amounted to $3.912 billion, a fall of 7 percent from October.
-- EMBRATEL WANTS TO CATCH UP

State-owned long distance telephone operator Embratel is cutting staff by 14 percent this year, has invested $850 million in 1996 and plans to invest $950 million next year to catch up with an increasingly competitive telecommunications market.
O GLOBO
-- CARDOSO'S POPULARITY IS ON THE RISE

A survey shows President Fernando Henrique Cardoso's popularity has grown to 61 percent in November from 49 percent in August, and only 29 percent of the 3,000 interviewed disapproved of his administration.
-- FIND OF WATER ON MOON COULD MAKE COLONIZATION POSSIBLE
The discovery of ice in a moon crater, which was announced by the U.S. Pentagon, indicates the existence of water on the moon and could make human colonization of the moon possible.
FOLHA DE SAO PAULO
-- STATE GOVT CHANGES RULES FOR GRANTING CONCESSIONS

The Sao Paulo state government has changed the criteria for choosing investors competing to acquire concessions to run state-owned businesses and will now take into consideration the quality of the technical proposals made.
-- SAO PAULO STUDENTS HAVE TO STUDY IN CONTAINERS
More than 13,000 students in Sao Paulo's state schools might have to start their classes in 1997 in containers because of a lack of classrooms.
Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
